label: late original-phase a/o/i/n/l/x/c input when the sequence starts with p/b/k/z/h or a digit
explanation: Fires only in the original (input) phase, never at the delimiter or during copy, and only from t>=3 (mostly t=4..8); the rate rises with orig_idx and is highest on the last 1-3 inputs before <DEL>, so longer sequences (L=8,9) carry most of the mass. The input token is almost always one of a, o, i, n, l, x, c (a strongest, ~35% of mass, then o, then i), and first occurrences dominate. Earlier context gates it strongly: the first token being p, b, k, z, h or a digit roughly doubles the rate, and more of those tokens earlier in the prefix helps too (n_seen>=3 as an alternative clause raises dev mass recall to 0.80 at precision 0.40). Top activations (~0.14-0.15) are a/o on the last step or second-to-last step of a 9-token sequence starting with p/b/2/3. Even with these conditions, many matching steps stay silent, so the gating looks like a distributed function of the prefix that the predicate only approximates. Dev: P 0.44, R 0.60, F1 0.51, mass recall 0.70. Never fires on t<3, the delimiter or copy-phase steps, and rarely on other letters such as r, f, d or digit inputs.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: a, o, i, n, l, x; least: 2, 3, q, p) and the first original token (most: p, 2, k, b, 1, 3; least: c, n, o, a); timing cues that raise it most: t=6, L=9 & t=8, t=7.
